raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment` emits at most one tool-call
unit per delta: a tool name with empty parameters, then that call's argument
diff, then the next call. When a final delta carries more than one complete
tool call (larger `--stream-interval`, multi-token decode steps), the
remainder is left stranded in `self._buffer`, and `BaseFormatDetector.finish()`
returns an empty result — the trailing calls are silently dropped. The
serving-side top-up (`_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args`) only covers argument
bytes of the last *tracked* call, so a stranded call is unrecoverable.

Reproduced offline with `FunctionCallParser` directly: streaming
`<tool_call>{...NYC...}</tool_call><tool_call>{...LA...}</tool_call>` as one
delta emits only `[(0, 'get_weather', '')]` — the argument bytes and the
second call are lost — while `detect_and_parse` returns both calls. With
fine-grained chunks the second call lands complete in the buffer and
disappears at flush. The same loss pattern was already fixed per-detector in
#31860 (Inkling) and #33901 (GLM-4.7), and is being patched
detector-by-detector in #36129/#40994/#41909/#41914. `JsonArrayParser.finish()`
already implements the drain pattern; the shared base default does not.

## Modifications

- `BaseFormatDetector.finish()`: re-run `parse_streaming_increment("")` until
  it stops emitting calls (identical to the existing
  `JsonArrayParser.finish()`), accumulating normal_text and calls.
  Termination: every call-emitting pass either consumes the completed call
  from the buffer or flips `current_tool_name_sent`. Detectors with their own
  `finish()` overrides are unaffected; normal streaming paths are unchanged
  because `finish()` is only called once at stream end.

## Tests

Offline unit tests (no server, no model loading), added to the existing
classes:

- `TestQwen25Detector.test_flush_drains_calls_stranded_in_final_chunk`: a
  final delta with two complete calls now yields both, and `finish()` is
  idempotent.
- `TestQwen25Detector.test_streaming_with_flush_matches_non_streaming`:
  streaming + flush equals `detect_and_parse` for chunk sizes 1 / 7 / full.
- `TestLlama32Detector.test_flush_drains_calls_stranded_in_final_chunk`.

A sweep of all 45 registered parsers (per-format text generated from each
detector's `structure_info()`, non-streaming oracle, chunk sizes 1/7/full,
30s timeout) goes fail→pass for qwen, qwen25, llama3, trinity, apertus2509
and strictly improves hermes (argument bytes recovered); all other results
are identical to unmodified main — no hangs, no regressions.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: no user-facing option changed)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A: pure parsing-logic fix, no kernel/model-forward changes)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

cc @JustinTong0323 (function_call codeowner). Note for #40994: with this base
fix, the Llama 3.2 flush case is covered; that PR can be rebased on top.

files.patch:
@@ -355,8 +355,25 @@ def finish(self, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult:
 
         Detectors that hold text back while waiting for a marker that can no
         longer arrive (the stream is over) override this to release it.
+
+        The default implementation also drains buffered tool calls: each
+        increment emits at most one tool-call unit (a name, then an argument
+        diff, then the next call), so a final delta that completes more than
+        one call strands the remainder in the buffer with no following delta
+        to pick it up. Re-running the increment until it stops emitting calls
+        flushes them, matching JsonArrayParser.finish(). This terminates
+        because every call-emitting pass either consumes the completed call
+        from the buffer or flips current_tool_name_sent.
         """
-        return StreamingParseResult()
+        normal_text = ""
+        calls: List[ToolCallItem] = []
+        while True:
+            result = self.parse_streaming_increment("", tools)
+            normal_text += result.normal_text
+            calls.extend(result.calls)
+            progress = [call for call in result.calls if call.name or call.parameters]
+            if not progress:
+                return StreamingParseResult(normal_text=normal_text, calls=calls)
 
     def supports_structural_tag(self) -> bool:
         """Return True if this detector supports structural tag format."""

@@ -5579,6 +5579,95 @@ def test_streaming_multiple_tool_calls_char_by_char_separator(self):
         cities = [json.loads(result[i]["parameters"])["city"] for i in sorted(result)]
         self.assertEqual(cities, ["NYC", "LA"])
 
+    def _collect_streaming_tool_calls_with_flush(self, chunks, tools=None):
+        """Helper: like _collect_streaming_tool_calls, plus the end-of-stream
+        finish() flush, so tool calls stranded in the buffer are not lost."""
+        tools = self.tools if tools is None else tools
+        tool_calls_by_index = {}
+        results = [
+            self.detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, tools) for chunk in chunks
+        ]
+        results.append(self.detector.finish(tools))
+        for result in results:
+            for call in result.calls:
+                entry = tool_calls_by_index.setdefault(
+                    call.tool_index, {"name": "", "parameters": ""}
+                )
+                if call.name:
+                    entry["name"] = call.name
+                if call.parameters:
+                    entry["parameters"] += call.parameters
+        return tool_calls_by_index
+
+    def test_flush_drains_calls_stranded_in_final_chunk(self):
+        """A final delta that carries several complete tool calls must not
+        lose the ones the one-action-per-increment parser could not reach:
+        finish() drains the remainder of the buffer."""
+        call1 = (
+            '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", '
+            '"arguments": {"city": "NYC", "state": "NY"}}\n</tool_call>'
+        )
+        call2 = (
+            '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", '
+            '"arguments": {"city": "LA", "state": "CA"}}\n</tool_call>'
+        )
+
+        result = self._collect_streaming_tool_calls_with_flush([call1 + call2])
+        self.assertEqual(len(result), 2, f"Expected 2 tool calls, got {len(result)}")
+        self.assertEqual(result[0]["name"], "get_current_weather")
+        self.assertEqual(result[1]["name"], "get_current_weather")
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result[0]["parameters"])["city"], "NYC")
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result[1]["parameters"])["city"], "LA")
+
+        # finish() must be idempotent.
+        self.assertEqual(self.detector.finish(self.tools).calls, [])
+
+    def test_streaming_with_flush_matches_non_streaming(self):
+        """Streaming plus the end-of-stream flush must reproduce the
+        non-streaming tool calls regardless of how the text is chunked."""
+        from sglang.srt.function_call.qwen25_detector import Qwen25Detector
+
+        tools = [
+            *self.tools,
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="get_time",
+                    description="Get the current time in a given timezone",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {"tz": {"type": "string"}},
+                        "required": ["tz"],
+                    },
+                ),
+            ),
+        ]
+        text = (
+            "Sure! "
+            '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", '
+            '"arguments": {"city": "NYC", "state": "NY"}}\n</tool_call>'
+            '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_time", '
+            '"arguments": {"tz": "UTC"}}\n</tool_call>'
+        )
+        self.detector = Qwen25Detector()
+        expected = [
+            (c.tool_index, c.name, json.loads(c.parameters))
+            for c in self.detector.detect_and_parse(text, tools).calls
+        ]
+
+        for size in (1, 7, len(text)):
+            with self.subTest(chunk_size=size):
+                self.detector = Qwen25Detector()
+                chunks = [text[i : i + size] for i in range(0, len(text), size)]
+                result = self._collect_streaming_tool_calls_with_flush(chunks, tools)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    [
+                        (i, e["name"], json.loads(e["parameters"]))
+                        for i, e in sorted(result.items())
+                    ],
+                    expected,
+                )
+
 
 class TestGemma4Detector(unittest.TestCase):
     def setUp(self):

@@ -185,6 +185,36 @@ def test_streaming_text_then_tool_call(self):
         self.assertEqual(params["city"], "Tokyo")
         self.assertEqual(params["unit"], "celsius")
 
+    def test_flush_drains_calls_stranded_in_final_chunk(self):
+        """A final delta that carries both complete tool calls must not lose
+        the second one: finish() drains what the increments left buffered."""
+        detector = Llama32Detector()
+        text = (
+            '<|python_tag|>{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Paris"}};'
+            '{"name": "search", "parameters": {"query": "hotels"}}'
+        )
+        all_calls = []
+        all_calls.extend(detector.parse_streaming_increment(text, self.tools).calls)
+        all_calls.extend(detector.finish(self.tools).calls)
+
+        streamed = {}
+        for call in all_calls:
+            entry = streamed.setdefault(call.tool_index, {"name": "", "arguments": ""})
+            entry["name"] += call.name or ""
+            entry["arguments"] += call.parameters
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [
+                (e["name"], json.loads(e["arguments"]))
+                for _, e in sorted(streamed.items())
+            ],
+            [
+                ("get_weather", {"city": "Paris"}),
+                ("search", {"query": "hotels"}),
+            ],
+        )
+        # finish() must be idempotent.
+        self.assertEqual(detector.finish(self.tools).calls, [])
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     import unittest
